elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence after the Base Components grant: "The foregoing license also extends to Customer's Affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf...". "Customer" is defined as Bluefly, Inc. only, so this is new coverage rather than duplication, and § 14.17's "only the licenses expressly specified herein" is satisfied because the affiliate extension is now expressly specified.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence expressly covers "contractors acting on Customer's behalf"; the retained anti-copy covenant does not contradict use by contractors on Customer's behalf.
§ 7.0(c) as rendered: "IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license ... copies of Type II Materials." "perpetual" is the only word added.
Already met and retained unaltered: "irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license" in § 7.0(c).

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: "revocable" struck from the Base Components grant and replaced by "IBM may terminate it only for Customer's uncured material breach" in the same inserted sentence, which attaches to "the foregoing license" (the Base Components licence). No at-will revocation language remains in the cited text.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Retained § 14.10: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition" — the Agreement (and therefore the licence rights granted under it) moves to the successor; no new Vendor-side assignment exception was created.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Exceeded in Customer's favour: affiliates are covered outright by the inserted sentence with no notice condition, so the fallback's notice-gated coverage is satisfied a fortiori.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Unchanged § 14.10 permits assignment "to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition".

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements are met in operative language (three by edit, two already met and retained, one — perpetuity — by a single-word insertion).

The "deviation" classification is correct on the original text: the Base Components grant was expressly "revocable" and ran to Bluefly, Inc. alone, with § 14.17 foreclosing implied affiliate/contractor rights, so the fallback (affiliates covered) failed and the clause sat at walk-away.

Minimality holds: exactly three surgical operations — delete "revocable", add one sentence carrying the affiliate/contractor extension plus the breach-only termination trigger, add "perpetual" to the Type II grant. No survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no procedures, no separate (and unnecessary) personnel/access edit, and no duplicate affiliate coverage since "Customer" is the single named entity. Favourable existing wording (irrevocable, worldwide, paid-up; the M&A assignment carve-out) is retained untouched.

Intent preserved: the "solely in connection with the Services", anti-reverse-engineering, one-backup-copy, "within Customer's Enterprise only", and assignment-consent mechanics all survive without contradiction; no cross-reference is left dangling.

Drafting nit for the drafter (not a level failure): "Affiliates" is capitalised but no Affiliate definition appears in the supplied text (the Agreement elsewhere uses "Customer's Enterprise"). To avoid an undefined defined-term argument, either lowercase it or add "(as defined in the Agreement/meaning any entity controlling, controlled by, or under common control with Customer)".

Second nit: the breach-only termination promise governs revocation of the licence itself; confirm no other termination or suspension provision elsewhere in the Base Terms lets IBM cut off Base Components use on other grounds, which would create a retained contradictory sentence.
